question: Is Nomex fabric safe to use inside a lunar habitat at 34% oxygen?
claim: PSI has no Nomex test at 34% oxygen: the 10 Nomex tests found (BASS-II, BASS, Saffire-II) reached at most 22.2% O2, so the data cannot say whether Nomex is safe or unsafe at 34% O2.
summary_student: NASA burned Nomex samples in space in 10 tests, but the most oxygen any of them had was 22.2%, close to normal air. None came near the 34% oxygen asked about for a lunar habitat. So these tests cannot tell us if Nomex is safe there; that would need new tests at higher oxygen.
summary_professional: Nomex appears in 10 microgravity tests: BASS-II (PSI-25, n = 3, O2 max 22.2%), BASS (PSI-26, n = 6, O2 not recorded in the table) and Saffire-II (PSI-99, n = 1, O2 approximately 22.1%, derived from measured CO2, combined PMMA and Nomex sample). The number of Nomex tests with O2 at or above 34% is 0 in every investigation. No Nomex row records ambient pressure, so the reduced lunar habitat pressure is also untested for this material.

params.sql: WITH n AS (SELECT * FROM tests WHERE lower(fuel) LIKE '%nomex%'), g AS (SELECT investigation, source_table, lower(replace(investigation, '-', '')) AS p, count(*) AS n_all, count(o2_pct_max) AS n_o2, max(o2_pct_max) AS o2_max, count(*) FILTER (WHERE o2_pct_max >= 34) AS n_hi, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS rows_all, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) FILTER (WHERE o2_pct_max IS NOT NULL) AS rows_o2, list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.fuel')) AS c_fuel, list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_max')) FILTER (WHERE o2_pct_max IS NOT NULL) AS c_o2 FROM n GROUP BY investigation, source_table) SELECT p || '_nomex_tests' AS name, n_all AS value, 'tests' AS unit, investigation, source_table, rows_all AS source_rows, c_fuel AS source_columns FROM g UNION ALL SELECT p || '_nomex_tests_with_o2', n_o2, 'tests', investigation, source_table, rows_all, c_fuel FROM g UNION ALL SELECT p || '_nomex_o2_max', o2_max, '% O2', investigation, source_table, rows_o2, c_o2 FROM g WHERE n_o2 > 0 UNION ALL SELECT p || '_nomex_tests_o2_at_or_above_34', n_hi, 'tests', investigation, source_table, rows_all, c_fuel FROM g UNION ALL SELECT 'o2_threshold_lunar_question', 34, '% O2', investigation, source_table, rows_o2, c_o2 FROM g WHERE investigation = 'PSI-25'

method.formula: The values returned by the SQL query in params, one row per value, each with the source rows it used.

assumptions: Every sample whose fuel name contains 'Nomex' (Nomex natural III, Nomex blend, PMMA & Nomex) was counted as Nomex.
The highest O2 value of each row (o2_pct_max) was compared with the 34% threshold from the question.
The Saffire-II O2 value is approximate and was derived from measured CO2 production, as the PSI table notes.
limitations: No Nomex test reached 34% O2, so this finding does not show that Nomex is safe or unsafe at that level; it only shows the gap in the data.
All Nomex tests were in microgravity; there is no lunar-gravity or Earth-gravity Nomex result in these tables.
No Nomex row records ambient pressure, so the effect of the reduced lunar habitat pressure cannot be judged.
The BASS (PSI-26) table gives no O2 value, so its 6 Nomex tests do not bound the oxygen level.
The Saffire-II test burned PMMA and Nomex together, so it is not a clean Nomex-only result.
Only PSI tables were searched; NASA material flammability tests outside PSI (for example NASA-STD-6001 results) are not included.
warnings: PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data. Lunar and Mars conclusions are bounded by microgravity and Earth-gravity results only.

chart.idea: Bars of the highest O2 at which Nomex was tested in BASS-II and Saffire-II, with a dashed line at the 34% O2 lunar habitat level from the question.
